knowledge_point.title: Computing an Integral Using the Sum Rule

question.:question/worked-solution:
Applying the sum rule, we compute the sum of the integrals of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \left(-x^{2}+5\right)\,\mathrm{d}x &= \int \left(-x^{2}+5\right)\,\mathrm{d}x \\ &= -\int x^{2}\,\mathrm{d}x+5\int 1\,\mathrm{d}x \\ &= -\frac{x^{2+1}}{(2+1)}+5\frac{x^{0+1}}{(0+1)}+C \\ &= -\frac{x^{3}}{3}+5x+C\end{aligned}
$$
